title: Cocartesian restriction to transport-stable full subcategories
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, full subcategories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cocartesian fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to S$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories in fixed universes. Let $R\subseteq E$ be a full subcategory, replete in $E$ (every object equivalent in $E$ to an object of $R$ belongs to $R$). Suppose that for every $x\in R$ and every edge $\alpha:p(x)\to s$ of $S$ there is a $p$-cocartesian lift $x\to y$ of $\alpha$ with $y\in R$. Then $p|_R:R\to S$ is a cocartesian fibration. An edge in $R$ is $(p|_R)$-cocartesian if and only if it is $p$-cocartesian in $E$; in particular the inclusion preserves and reflects these edges.
For every small simplicial set $K$ and fixed $a:K\to S$, define $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(K,E)$ as the degreewise fiber of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)$ over $a$, and similarly for $R$. These fibers are quasicategories, and the inclusion
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(K,R)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(K,E)$$
is the full subcategory on diagrams all of whose object values belong to $R$. Its right-pinched mapping simplicial sets are the same degreewise as those of the ambient relative functor category. This description is natural under precomposition in $K$, including the empty simplicial set.

source.place: step 5, full-image fibration and strict relative functor inclusion (HTT Proposition 2.4.4.3, dual mapping-space criterion, and Proposition 3.1.2.1, dual cocartesian exponentiation). Agent-formulated lemma extracted from the retained proof, not a verbatim source theorem. The indicated source is not archived in literature; WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Put $q=p|_R$. A filler in $E$ of an inner horn in $R$ has exactly the vertices already present in that horn, because $n\geq2$ and every vertex of $\Delta^n$ belongs to $\Lambda_i^n$. All these vertices belong to $R$, so fullness puts the entire filler in $R$. Applying this first to the quasicategory $E$, and then to a specified lifting problem over $S$ for the inner fibration $p$, proves respectively that $R$ is a quasicategory and $q$ is an inner fibration.

source.place: Definitions 2.0.0.3 and 2.4.2.1; elementary full-subset horn calculation

proof.text: If an edge $u$ in $R$ is $p$-cocartesian, solve any of its defining $\Lambda_0^n$ lifting problems in $E$. Again $n\geq2$, so the horn contains every vertex; its filler lies in $R$ by fullness. Hence $u$ is $q$-cocartesian. The assumed lift with source $x\in R$ and target in $R$ is an edge of $R$, again by fullness, and is therefore a $q$-cocartesian lift over the prescribed base edge. Together with step 1 this proves that $q$ is a cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.4 and Definition 2.4.2.1, opposite dual; direct horn argument

proof.text: For reflection let $e:x\to y$ in $R$ be $q$-cocartesian and put $\alpha=p(e)$. Choose the lift $u:x\to y_0$ over exactly $\alpha$ supplied by the hypothesis, with $y_0\in R$ and $u$ $p$-cocartesian. Step 2 makes $u$ $q$-cocartesian. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to $q$: both $u$ and $e$ are initial objects of $L_q(x,\alpha)$, so their comparison gives a triangle with edges $u$, $v:y_0\to y$, $e$, where $q(v)$ is the degenerate identity at $p(y)$ and $v$ is an equivalence in the fiber. Its inverse and inverse triangles are also in $E$, so $v$ is an equivalence in $E$. The initial-outer-horn assertion of [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift], applied to the inner fibration $p$ and this equivalence $v$, gives every defining horn filler for $v$: thus $v$ is $p$-cocartesian. Now apply the composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to the same triangle in $E$. Since $u$ and $v$ are $p$-cocartesian, so is $e$. This proves reflection, and step 2 proves preservation.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.7 and Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite duals; Proposition 2.4.1.5 for the equivalence-edge case, implemented by the cited relative outer-horn lemma

proof.text: For $Z=E,R$ put $p_Z=p,q$, respectively. A lifting problem for $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)$ against an inner horn is, by the degreewise exponential definition, exactly a lifting problem for $p_Z$ against $K\times\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow K\times\Delta^n$. An inner horn inclusion has the left lifting property against every inner fibration, by the definition of inner fibration. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] to it and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$: the indicated product inclusion is inner anodyne, and hence has the left lifting property against $p_Z$. Thus the postcomposition map is an inner fibration. Pulling it back degreewise over the constant vertex $a:K\to S$ gives the stated strict fiber. To fill an inner horn of this fiber, use the constant base simplex at $a$ in the lifting problem just solved. The resulting filler still has that exact base simplex. Consequently each strict fiber is a quasicategory. This argument applies to arbitrary small simplicial $K$, without requiring that $K$ be a quasicategory.

source.place: Corollary 2.3.2.4 (inner-anodyne products) and the inner-fibration consequence of the dual of Proposition 3.1.2.1; exponential adjunction written out

proof.text: Write $T_Z=\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(K,Z)$. Its $n$-simplices are exactly maps $h:K\times\Delta^n\to Z$ with $p_Zh=a\operatorname{pr}_K$. Such an $h$ valued in $E$ factors through $R$ if and only if every vertex $h(k,i)$ belongs to $R$, by the definition of a full simplicial subcategory. For fixed $i$, these are precisely the object values of the diagram obtained by restriction to $K\times\{i\}$. Therefore the inclusion $T_R\hookrightarrow T_E$ is degreewise injective and consists of precisely those simplices all of whose diagram vertices take their object values in $R$. This is exactly the asserted full subcategory.

source.place: Elementary calculation with the degreewise exponential and full-subcategory definitions

proof.text: Fix diagrams $b,c\in T_R$. An $n$-simplex of the right-pinched mapping simplicial set in $T_E$ is a map $\Delta^{n+1}\to T_E$ whose entire initial face is constant at $b$ and whose last vertex is $c$. Its vertices are all $b$ or $c$. Step 5 therefore puts the whole simplex in $T_R$, and its initial-face and last-vertex conditions are unchanged. The reverse inclusion is immediate, so these mapping simplicial sets are equal degreewise, with identical operators. For $t:L\to K$, restriction sends $h$ to $h\circ(t\times\mathrm{id})$, with base $at$; this preserves the vertex condition and commutes with every parameter restriction, including those defining the pinched mapping spaces. Thus the descriptions commute with precomposition. If $K=\varnothing$, each product $K\times\Delta^n$ is empty and each strict fiber is the one-point simplicial set; both inclusions and their mapping-space equalities are identities, so the assertion includes this case.

source.place: Elementary full-subcategory, right-pinched mapping-space and precomposition calculations

tool_uses.why: The relative outer-horn filler along an equivalence is a generic quasicategory tool used only to recognize the comparison equivalence as p-cocartesian; the item unit has no separate equivalence-edge horn assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q99-c66f142f6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item (statement and all six steps), the statement of every cited node, the unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, the blueprint ancestor prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint (proof paragraph 2) and the only citer, lem-coef-monoidal-yoneda-embedding (steps 9 and 10). The delivery is one commit containing the item and its report. It adds no new nodes and changes neither statement nor stmt_deps. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, there is no cycle, nothing cites a merged node and nothing cites SGA. Steps 1 and 2 are elementary and correct: for n>=2 every horn Λ^n_i contains all vertices, so by fullness the inner-horn and Λ^n_0 fillers stay in R. Step 3 is correct. Both u and e are initial lifts in L_q(x,α), and the cited composition-initiality statement gives the comparison 2-simplex (u,v,e) with v over 1_b and v an equivalence in the fiber, so v is also an equivalence in E. The relative outer-horn lemma then makes v p-cocartesian, and the composition clause applied to p makes e p-cocartesian. Step 4 is correct: the pushout-product Mathlib leaf with Λ^n_i→Δ^n and ∅→K shows Fun(K,Z)→Fun(K,S) is an inner fibration, and the constant base simplex makes each strict fiber a quasicategory for any small K. Steps 5 and 6 are correct: the vertices of K×Δ^n are pairs (k,i), so T_R is exactly the full subcategory of R-valued diagrams; the pinched mapping simplices have only b or c as vertices, so the mapping sets are equal; precomposition commutes with all of this; and K=∅ gives point fibers. Edge cases tested: R empty, R=E, S a point, nerves, identity base edges, K empty and K a point. Repleteness is retained but unused; nothing is weakened. The outer-horn lemma assumes small quasicategories, but the argument does not depend on size, so this is a remark, not a fault. HTT is not archived; it is listed as WANTED and the proof is marked as agent-written. I checked 2.4.1.5, 2.4.1.7, 2.3.2.4 and 3.1.2.1 from memory and they fit. The duplicate search turned up only the sk-prop-sf-cbc outer-horn pair, of which the relative one is the node cited, and the mapping-space-based pointwise-transport node, which uses a different notion and is not a duplicate. Accepted tool_use: lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift in step 3 only, as generic relative outer-horn filling along an equivalence. No fixes.
